knowledge_weighting.method: entry-weighted mean of O*NET 31.0 importance (Scale IM): entry targets weight 2; other linked occupations in Job Zone 4 or 5 (or the entry targets' Job Zone) weight 1; Manager, Chief, Postsecondary-faculty, All Other, Supervisor, Director and Treasurers and Controllers titles, and non-target occupations in other Job Zones, weight 0
knowledge_weighting.note: top_knowledge/top_skills are the unweighted mean over all linked occupations (kept for comparison); the outline uses the entry-weighted lists.

skipped_knowledge.reason: ranked below the knowledge areas the outline already covers (the outline gives at most six course slots to knowledge); worth an elective if a target role needs it

outline_elements.rule: English Language is placed in Year 1 general education; workplace and management elements (Customer and Personal Service, Administrative, Clerical, Administration and Management, Personnel and Human Resources, Education and Training) get no course slot unless the major's CIP series is about them; the next three elements go to Year 2 and up to three more (ordered by importance to the entry targets) to Year 3; if fewer than two remain for Year 3, knowledge rated at least 2.5 for the entry targets fills it

method.supervisory_tasks: task statement matches a supervisory/managerial pattern (supervise, provide supervision, direct and coordinate, direct the work/activities/staff of, manage staff/personnel/employees/workers/teams, oversee the work/staff, hire, subordinates, assign work to, evaluate the work/performance of, train and supervise); 'under supervision' does not count

quality_flags.note: Authored tier: entry targets and practice tasks were chosen and reviewed per major, so the generated-tier plausibility flags are not applied. Informational only: cited tasks whose O*NET statement is supervisory are listed; their authored scenarios say when they are practice for a later or graduate role.

entry_target_basis: Job Zone 4 linked occupations (excluding Manager/Chief/Postsecondary/All Other/Supervisor/Director/Treasurers and Controllers titles), ranked by similarity of their O*NET knowledge-importance profile to the average profile of the eligible linked occupations (Pearson correlation), base O*NET-SOC .00 codes first; then a documented DreamCo manual override (authored/target_overrides.json) changed the rule output (13-2031.00, 13-2041.00, 13-2072.00) to 13-2051.00, 13-2041.00, 13-2072.00

entry_target_review.reason: Financial and Investment Analysts, the most typical entry role for finance graduates, was missing from the rule output. Budget Analysts was dropped here (it remains a target for Accounting, where budget work is closer to the curriculum). Credit Analysts and Loan Officers are kept.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A regional coffee-roasting company (invented figures: revenue 12 million, EBITDA 1.8 million, debt 3 million) is deciding whether to buy a competitor for 6 million funded by a new term loan, expecting 400,000 in yearly cost savings after year one. Build a simple model (describe its structure and show key numbers): pro forma revenue and EBITDA, debt and leverage ratios, interest coverage, and a five-year discounted cash flow or payback view of the deal. Write a memo with your conclusion and a sensitivity table for savings and interest rate.

rubric.description: Model has clear inputs, calculations and outputs, with assumptions stated and kept separate.
Leverage, coverage and valuation figures are computed correctly and consistently.
Sensitivity analysis shows how the conclusion changes under plausible downside cases.

reference_answer_outline: Inputs tab: prices, growth, savings ramp, loan rate and term.
Pro forma EBITDA combined plus synergies; leverage equals total debt over EBITDA.
Interest coverage equals EBITDA over interest; compare with lender comfort ranges.
Net present value of incremental cash flows minus price; payback years.
Sensitivity grid of savings achieved versus interest rate; recommendation with conditions.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented case: a regional bank is asked for a 2 million working-capital line by an auto-parts distributor whose largest customer accounts for 35 percent of sales, whose inventory has grown faster than sales, and whose current ratio fell from 1.8 to 1.3 in two years. Write the credit risk report: business and industry overview, financial ratio analysis (liquidity, leverage, efficiency), qualitative risks, a risk rating on a stated scale with justification, and the structure and covenants that would make the risk acceptable.

rubric.description: Uses relevant ratios (current ratio, inventory days, debt to equity, coverage) and interprets trends, not just levels.
Recognizes customer concentration and inventory build-up as key risks and assesses their potential impact.
Proposes structure (borrowing base, covenants, reporting) that directly addresses the identified risks.

reference_answer_outline: Overview: products, customers, supplier terms, cyclical auto sector.
Ratios: declining liquidity, rising inventory days, leverage trend.
Concentration risk: impact if the top customer leaves.
Rating with rationale on the bank's scale.
Structure: borrowing base tied to receivables and inventory with advance rates, minimum coverage covenant, monthly aging reports.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You are a loan officer with authority to approve consumer auto loans up to 40,000 with debt-to-income up to 43 percent and credit scores of 660 and above. Three invented applications arrive: (A) 28,000, DTI 38 percent, score 702; (B) 45,000, DTI 31 percent, score 760; (C) 22,000, DTI 46 percent, score 690 with a recent job change. Write a decision memo for each: approve, decline, or refer, with reasons tied to policy, any conditions, and how the referral to your manager is documented. Add a note on fair lending consistency.

rubric.description: Approves only within limits, refers B for amount, and handles C's DTI exception properly (refer or decline per policy).
Each decision cites the specific policy criteria and any compensating factors.
Applies criteria consistently regardless of protected characteristics and documents referrals and exceptions.

reference_answer_outline: A: within all limits; approve with standard verification of income and insurance.
B: strong credit but over the 40,000 limit; refer to the manager with a recommendation.
C: DTI above policy; refer as an exception with compensating factors or decline with an adverse action notice.
Referral memo: summary, policy exception, recommendation.
Fair lending: same criteria and documentation for every applicant.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Prepare a 10-minute investment-committee briefing on one publicly traded industry you choose (for example, regional airlines, or solar equipment). Using public sources (annual reports, government statistics, industry data), cover: current industry drivers, two companies compared on growth, margins and leverage, key risks over the next two years, and your view. Deliver it as slide titles with key points plus a one-page written summary, with every figure cited.

rubric.description: Uses cited, current public data and distinguishes facts from forecasts and opinions.
Company comparison uses consistent metrics and explains differences.
Ends with a defensible view, key risks, and what evidence would change the view.

reference_answer_outline: Industry drivers such as fuel costs, demand trends, regulation or interest rates.
Comparison table: revenue growth, operating margin, debt to EBITDA, free cash flow.
Risks: cyclical demand, input costs, policy changes.
View: overweight, neutral or underweight with reasoning.
Sources listed with dates.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented case: a commercial customer of a bank says three wire transfers totaling 18,000 on its statement were never authorized, and also disputes a fee for exceeding its credit-line limit. As the credit analyst on the relationship team, write the procedure you would follow: immediate steps to protect the account, how you verify each transaction (authorization logs, callbacks, IP or device records), how the over-limit fee is reviewed, communication with the customer at each stage, and the final resolution letter.

rubric.description: Secures the account promptly (block, credential reset) and escalates potential fraud to the right team.
Checks authorization evidence for each transfer and reviews the fee against the credit agreement and actual balances.
Gives the customer timelines and a professional, specific resolution letter.

reference_answer_outline: Freeze online wire capability; refer to the fraud team; preserve records.
Pull wire authorization logs, approval user IDs, callback records, device data.
Fee review: compare balances with the line limit and agreement terms; reverse if posted in error.
Update the customer within set timeframes.
Letter stating findings, any credits, and security recommendations such as dual approval.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A first-time home buyer couple, both in their twenties with one gig-economy income and one salaried income, books a meeting to apply for a mortgage. Write your interview guide: the information and documents you need (and why for each), how you explain the steps from application to closing, the questions they are likely to ask (down payment, rate locks, credit checks) with plain-language answers, how you handle variable gig income, and the follow-up checklist you hand them.

rubric.description: Lists the documents and data needed and explains why, including how variable income is documented.
Explains the stages and timelines accurately in plain language.
Answers questions without steering or promising approval, and gives a clear follow-up checklist.

reference_answer_outline: Documents: ID, pay stubs, W-2s or tax returns, two years of 1099 and bank statements for gig income, asset statements.
Process: application, disclosures, appraisal, underwriting, conditions, closing.
Explain rate locks, down payment options, and credit inquiry effects.
Gig income: typically averaged over two years; explain why.
Checklist with dates and contact information.
